correctness.rationale: For every bounded complete trajectory, backward variation of constants in \(\dot y+y=x^2\) gives \(y(t)=\int_0^\infty e^{-s}x(t-s)^2ds\ge0\); equality would force an entire past half-orbit with \(x=y=0\), contradicting boundedness because then \(\dot z=1\). Thus compact invariant support lies in \(y>0\). Generator stationarity applied to arbitrary one-coordinate C1 primitives gives the three conditional expectation laws. Their expectations yield \(E[x]=1/4\), \(E[y]=E[x^2]\), and hence the exact variance defect. Equality forces the unique equilibrium. Finally, if a non-equilibrium invariant measure lived in one closed z-half-space, \(y>0\) and \(\int yz=0\) would force \(z=0\), then invariance forces the equilibrium; periodic sign crossing follows by continuity. The bundled exact-arithmetic checker independently confirms the equilibrium algebra but is not used for the measure-theoretic proof.

These statements apply to every compact invariant probability measure and immediately constrain every periodic or recurrent compact state, so they are structurally motivated rather than a numerical attractor observation.
